archetype.name: Pocket Passer (accuracy-first, sack-prone)
archetype.definition: A 36-year-old rhythm thrower who wins with ball placement and well-timed shots from the pocket, adds almost nothing with his legs, and has always held the ball into sacks.

report.headline: Accurate, sack-prone, and living on deep shots that won't stay this hot.
report.take:
Geno Smith in his 14th season looks a lot like the Seattle version again, not the 2025 Raiders version. Last year he posted -0.1 EPA per play (49th of 63) with 17 interceptions. This year he is completing 68.9% (8th), with a CPOE of +2.76, a 7.55 yards per attempt that is up 0.8 on last season, and a 9% bad-throw rate that ranks 6th. Clean placement has been the steady part of his game for years; in 2024 his bad-throw rate ranked 1st in the league. What has changed is that the throws aren't ending up with defenders: 1 interception in 177 attempts.

The season is being carried by a thin slice of plays. His 42 throws of 10+ air yards produced 33.4 EPA, while his 134 throws under 10 produced 16.2. The 16 deep attempts alone account for 25.2 EPA and 4 touchdowns. Garrett Wilson is the other pillar, at 0.479 EPA per target on 49 targets. Away from Wilson and the deep ball, the offense struggles. The tight end, Kenyon Sadiq, and the back, Braelon Allen, are both negative per target. Screens and throws behind the line are losing value. A run game ranked 23rd in EPA leaves him facing 8.9 yards to go on third down.

The yardage hides two problems. First, the sacks: 9.7% of dropbacks (38th of 45), and 40% of his pressures end in sacks (35th of 37). That isn't new. He was at 46.2% last year and 35.5% in 2024, and the Jets' line ranks 28th in hit rate allowed. Those sacks land in the worst places: 9 on third down and 4 in the red zone, where he is at -11.3 EPA. Second, his efficiency in close games is flat: 0.001 EPA a play within one score, -0.297 in close fourth quarters. Much of the shine comes from early-season blowups and trailing-by-9 stretches.

The last three games show how fragile this is. Against Chicago and Cleveland, two top-10 defenses today, his bad-throw rates spiked to 33.3% and 20.7% and he lost a combined 16 EPA. That pulled his last-three EPA per dropback to -0.121 and his CPOE to -5.6. New England was a partial rebound. Miami is the softest pass rush in the league, which suits him, but he goes in without Adonai Mitchell, Breece Hall and guard Dylan Parham. Expect a mid-pack starter whose interception count drifts back toward his career norm.

strengths.title: Placement and completion accuracy
strengths.body: He completes 68.9% with a 9% bad-throw rate, both top-10. His bad-throw rate has ranked in the top 5 three times in the last four seasons. This is the most durable part of his game, and it is why he can run a short, on-time passing game even behind a shaky line. It should hold, though the Chicago and Cleveland games show it can crack when pressure arrives fast.

strengths.title: Downfield shots are hitting
strengths.body: Throws of 10+ air yards are worth 0.795 EPA each, and the 20+ yard balls carry a +25 CPOE with 4 touchdowns. He picks his spots, with a 16.38% aggressiveness rate, and the payoff has been big. The skill is real, but 16 deep attempts is a hint rather than a fact. A 56% completion rate on deep balls with that kind of EPA will cool.

strengths.title: The Wilson connection
strengths.body: Garrett Wilson has 49 targets at 0.479 EPA per target, worth 23.5 EPA. That is the offense's single reliable engine. Throws to the middle, where Wilson and the slot work, return 0.733 EPA a play. As long as Wilson stays healthy this production has a floor.

concerns.title: Sacks, a career-long habit
concerns.body: His 9.7% sack rate ranks 38th of 45, and 40% of his pressures become sacks. That is in line with his 46.2% last year, so it isn't bad luck. It comes from a 2.95-second time to throw and a line that ranks 28th in hit rate allowed. The sacks cluster on third down and in the red zone, which is why a QB this accurate sits only 23rd in EPA per dropback. It is the price of how he plays and won't go away; the pace is 54 sacks.

concerns.title: Red zone and third down stall
concerns.body: He is at -11.3 EPA in the red zone and -0.121 per play on third down, converting just 32.7%. Average distance on third down is 8.9 yards, a product of a weak run game, and he tends to throw short of the sticks. His CPOE in both areas is positive, so the accuracy isn't failing. The problem is sacks and checkdowns. Without Breece Hall the long third downs likely continue.

concerns.title: Interception luck will fade
concerns.body: One interception, a 0.6% rate, against 17 last year and 15 in 2024. Some of that drop is real, since his bad throws are down 1.9 points from last season. Most of it is luck that won't hold, and he also has 4 turnover-worthy fumbles with 2 lost. Expect the turnover line to get worse even if his play doesn't.

trend.note: Weeks 1-3 were sharp, worth 9.8, 4.3 and 10.9 EPA. Pressure-heavy losses of efficiency against Chicago and Cleveland followed at -4.9 and -11.3, and a 5.9-EPA rebound in New England. That leaves his last three at -0.121 EPA per dropback, well under the season.

nextGame.headline: The league's weakest pass rush meets his biggest flaw
nextGame.body:
Miami is about as good a matchup as his profile gets. The Dolphins have the league's lowest sack rate (32nd) and rank 23rd in hit rate, so the main thing dragging his EPA down should ease. Their pass defense is 31st in EPA allowed and 30th on short throws, which suits a QB who lives under 10 air yards. Their WR1 number looks stingy in fantasy terms, but they still allow 0.42 EPA per WR1 target (24th). Tight ends are the hole, allowing the most EPA per target in the league. The catch is volume: a 38.5 total and a Miami offense that runs far more than expected point to a short game, and a 4.5-point lead late means handoffs.

Availability cuts against the Jets. Adonai Mitchell, a productive second receiver at 0.576 EPA per target, is out after finger surgery, so Isaiah Williams and Sadiq have to carry more. Breece Hall is out, which leaves a weak run game on Allen and means more long third downs. Dylan Parham, an 86%-snap guard, is out, which weakens interior protection even against a soft rush. On Miami's side, CB JuJu Brents (stinger), safety Michael Taaffe (chest) and CB Storm Duck (knee) all carry statuses that date to Oct. 11. If either starter in the secondary sits, Wilson and the middle of the field open up further.

keyMatchups.title: Protection versus a non-existent rush
keyMatchups.body: Miami gets home on 2.5% of dropbacks, the fewest in the league. Smith takes sacks on 9.7% of his. If the Jets' line, minus Parham, can win even routinely, his EPA per dropback should climb back toward his early-season level. A sacky game here would mean the problem is mostly his own.

keyMatchups.title: Sadiq against the softest TE defense
keyMatchups.body: Miami allows 0.9 EPA per tight end target (32nd) and gives TE1s 4.1 PPR over their averages. Sadiq has been a drain at -0.246 EPA per target on 24 looks. With Mitchell out, this is the chance for the tight end to stop costing the offense.

keyMatchups.title: Low total, run-heavy opponent
keyMatchups.body: The total is 38.5, and Miami's offense ranks 31st in pass rate over expected and 29th in EPA. Expect few possessions and a Jets team that leans on a 2nd-ranked run defense to sit on a lead. That caps his attempts even if the efficiency is strong.

nextGame.watch: His sack count. If Miami's league-worst rush still gets him down three or more times without Parham, the protection problem is structural and his ceiling stays capped all year.

restOfSeason.body:
The accuracy and Wilson connection are real and should keep him around 220 yards a game with a solid completion rate. Two things will move against him. His 0.6% interception rate is far below anything in his career, and he threw 17 last year. And his deep-ball EPA on 16 attempts is the kind of number that settles down. Sacks are part of who he is, so expect his EPA per dropback to land closer to league average than to his early-season form.

My ranges: 200-245 passing yards a game, 1.0-1.6 passing touchdowns, 2.6-3.6 sacks and 0.4-0.8 interceptions. That's a QB2-level fantasy line with little rushing help. Mitchell, Hall and Parham are expected back after this week, which matters. Mitchell gives him a second downfield option, and Hall could shorten third downs, the cleanest path to fixing the red-zone and third-down numbers.
swingFactors: Whether the deep-ball hit rate holds
Garrett Wilson's health and Mitchell's return

confidence.note: Six games, key splits on tiny samples (16 deep attempts), and three offensive starters out this week.
